31.text: The shamanistic “spirits” are for the most part material objects of various

32.text: kinds, — animals, such as wolves, reindeer, walrus, whales; birds; plants;

33.text: icebergs; household utensils, such as pots, hammers, needles, and needle-cases.

34.text: The chamber-vessel and urine are also shamans’ “spirits.” I was told of an

35.text: old man who met a fox defecating in the open (see Fig. 212, d). The fox

36.text: ran away, and the old man took its excrement for his own “spirit.” Another

37.text: old man, when practising shamanism, called his own penis as a “spirit.”

38.text: Sometimes household objects, etc., are described as calling, without invitation,

39.text: on the shaman during a manifestation. They put on mysterious airs, and

40.text: assume fine-sounding names. The needle, for instance, appears as a man,

41.text: and calls itself “the long one” (iwčuˊwg̣i). The work-bag is called by other
